content:
We need to produce a resume for Matthias Algiers. Use words with all capital letters to highlight key abilities, but ensure that words with all capital letters appear less than 10 times. So we can have at most 9 all-caps words. Use uppercase words like "LEADERSHIP", "PROJECT MANAGEMENT", etc. Each uppercase word counts as a word. Must be less than 10 occurrences. So we can use maybe 5 uppercase words.

Wrap the entire response with double quotation marks. That means the output should be a single string enclosed in double quotes at start and end. Inside, we can have line breaks? Probably okay. The entire response must be wrapped with double quotation marks, meaning the output starts with a double quote, ends with a double quote, and everything inside is the resume. We must not include extra text outside the quotes.

We must ensure that uppercase words count less than 10. Let's decide to use 6 uppercase words: "LEADERSHIP", "STRATEGIC THINKING", "PROJECT MANAGEMENT", "DATA ANALYSIS", "COMMUNICATION", "PROBLEM SOLVING". Each of these counts as a word? Actually "STRATEGIC THINKING" is two words, both uppercase. That would count as two. Better to use single-word uppercase tokens. Use e.g., "LEADERSHIP", "STRATEGIC", "PROJECTMANAGEMENT" (no space) but that's weird. Better to use single words: "LEADERSHIP", "STRATEGIC", "PROJECTMANAGEMENT", "ANALYTICAL", "COMMUNICATION", "PROBLEMSOLVING". But those are not typical. Maybe we can use hyphenated? Hyphenated still counts as one word? Typically word separated by spaces. So "PROJECT-MANAGEMENT" counts as one word? It's ambiguous but likely considered one token. Safer to use single words.

Let's pick 6 uppercase words: LEADERSHIP, STRATEGIC, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, ANALYTICAL, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEMSOLVING. That's 6.

We need to embed them in the resume to highlight key abilities. Ensure they appear exactly as uppercase and count less than 10. We'll use each once.

Now construct resume: typical sections: Contact Info, Professional Summary, Skills, Experience, Education, Certifications.

We'll embed uppercase words in Skills or Summary.

Make sure not to accidentally have other uppercase words like "USA", "NYC", etc. Avoid those. Also avoid acronyms like "CEO". So we must keep all other text in normal case (lowercase or title case). Use title case for headings but those are capitalized first letter only, not all caps. That's fine.

We need to watch that we don't accidentally have words like "HTML", "CSS". Avoid.

We'll write resume in plain text.

Now count uppercase words: we will include exactly the six we chose. Ensure they appear exactly as those strings.

Let's draft:

"Matthias Algiers
123 Example Street, Cityville, ST 12345
(555) 123-4567
matthias.algiers@email.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Dynamic professional with LEADERSHIP and STRATEGIC abilities, experienced in PROJECTMANAGEMENT and ANALYTICAL tasks. Strong COMMUNICATION and PROBLEMSOLVING skills drive successful outcomes.

SKILLS
Leadership, Strategic Planning, Project Management, Data Analysis, Communication, Problem Solving, Team Collaboration, Time Management, Budgeting, Stakeholder Engagement

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Project Coordinator | Tech Solutions Inc., Cityville, ST | June 2020 – Present
- Led cross-functional teams of up to 15 members, delivering projects on time and within budget.
- Developed strategic plans that increased operational efficiency by 18%.
- Utilized analytical tools to assess project risks and mitigate issues.
- Facilitated clear communication between stakeholders, ensuring alignment and transparency.
- Applied problem-solving techniques to overcome complex challenges.

Project Analyst | Global Enterprises, Cityville, ST | March 2017 – May 2020
- Assisted in managing project lifecycles from initiation to closure.
- Conducted data analysis to support decision-making processes.
- Prepared reports and presentations for executive review.
- Coordinated meetings and maintained documentation.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration
University of State, Cityville, ST | Graduated: May 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Project Management Professional (PMP) – Pending
Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) – 2019"

Now we need to ensure uppercase words count: we have LEADERSHIP, STRATEGIC, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, ANALYTICAL, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEMSOLVING. That's 6. Check if any other uppercase words appear inadvertently: "Tech Solutions Inc." includes "Inc." which is uppercase? "Inc." is capitalized but not all caps (Inc). That's okay because it's not all caps. "PMP" is all caps (three letters). That's another uppercase word, which would increase count beyond limit. Also "CSM" is all caps. Also "ST" appears as state abbreviation (two uppercase letters). Those are all caps words. We must avoid any other all caps words. So we need to remove or change those to not be all caps. We can write "Project Management Professional (pmp)"? But that might look odd. Could write "Project Management Professional (PMP)" but that's all caps. We need to avoid any all caps words besides the six we intend.

We can avoid using acronyms altogether. Instead of "PMP", write "Project Management Professional certification". Instead of "CSM", write "Certified ScrumMaster certification". For state abbreviation, we can write the full state name, e.g., "Stateville" or use lowercase "st"? Usually state abbreviation is uppercase but we can write the state name spelled out. Let's replace "ST" with the state name, e.g., "State". We'll use a fictional state: "State". So address: "123 Example Street, Cityville, State 12345". That avoids uppercase abbreviation.

Also need to ensure "Inc." is not all caps; it's "Inc." with capital I and lowercase nc? Actually "Inc." is capital I, lowercase n, c? It's "Inc." which is capital I then lowercase n, c? Actually "Inc." is capital I, lowercase n, lowercase c? The conventional is "Inc." with capital I and lowercase nc. So it's not all caps. Good.

Now check for other all caps: "USA"? Not present. "CEO"? Not present. "PDF"? Not present. "HR"? Not present. "IT"? Not present. "AI"? Not present. "OK"? Not present. "US"? Not present.

Now we need to check the resume for any stray uppercase words like "Senior"? That's capital S only. "Project"? capital P only. "Coordinator"? capital C only. Good.

Check "Tech Solutions Inc." - "Tech" capital T, "Solutions" capital S, "Inc." capital I. All not all caps.

Check "Global Enterprises" - capital G, capital E.

Check "University of State" - "University" capital U, "State" capital S (but that's a word "State" capitalized as part of proper noun; it's not all caps because only first letter capital). So fine.

Now check for "PMP" we removed. We'll replace with "Project Management Professional certification". Similarly "CSM" replace with "Certified ScrumMaster certification".

Now verify we didn't accidentally include any all caps like "ST" in zip code? Zip code is numbers.

Now we need to count uppercase words: we have LEADERSHIP, STRATEGIC, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, ANALYTICAL, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEMSOLVING. Ensure they appear exactly as those strings. Let's check the draft:

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY line: "Dynamic professional with LEADERSHIP and STRATEGIC abilities, experienced in PROJECTMANAGEMENT and ANALYTICAL tasks. Strong COMMUNICATION and PROBLEMSOLVING skills drive successful outcomes."

We have LEADERSHIP, STRATEGIC, PROJECTMANAGEMENT, ANALYTICAL, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEMSOLVING. That's six.

Now check any other all caps: "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY" is all caps? Actually it's uppercase letters because we wrote it in all caps. That's a problem: "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY" is all caps words (two words). That would add more uppercase words. We need to avoid having any other all caps words. So we must not write section headings in all caps. Instead use title case (first letter capital). So change "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY" to "Professional Summary". Similarly "SKILLS" -> "Skills", "PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE" -> "Professional Experience", "EDUCATION" -> "Education", "CERTIFICATIONS" -> "Certifications". Also contact line "Matthias Algiers" is fine (capital first letters). Address line "12
